title: Cannot build image on macOS through podman machine
body:
### Issue Description

```sh
$ cat Containerfile
FROM fedora
RUN dnf install -y perf runc procps-ng binutils less lsof psmisc sysstat vim zip util-linux && dnf clean all
$ podman build --platform linux/amd64 -t perfcontainer .
ERRO[0679] failed to close build request body: 1 error occurred:
	* open /Users/kevin/Library/Application Support/FileProvider/19467A89-FC03-40AE-BEAB-3D004245812B/wharf/tombstone/a: permission denied

 
Error: Post "http://d/v6.0.2/libpod/build?compressionFormat=gzip&dockerfile=%5B%22Containerfile%22%5D&forceCompressionFormat=1&forcerm=1&httpproxy=1&idmappingoptions=%7B%22HostUIDMapping%22%3Atrue%2C%22HostGIDMapping%22%3Atrue%2C%22UIDMap%22%3A%5B%5D%2C%22GIDMap%22%3A%5B%5D%2C%22AutoUserNs%22%3Afalse%2C%22AutoUserNsOpts%22%3A%7B%22Size%22%3A0%2C%22InitialSize%22%3A0%2C%22PasswdFile%22%3A%22%22%2C%22GroupFile%22%3A%22%22%2C%22AdditionalUIDMappings%22%3Anull%2C%22AdditionalGIDMappings%22%3Anull%7D%7D&inheritannotations=1&isolation=0&jobs=1&layers=1&networkmode=0&nsoptions=%5B%7B%22Name%22%3A%22user%22%2C%22Host%22%3Atrue%2C%22Path%22%3A%22%22%7D%5D&omithistory=0&output=perfcontainer&outputformat=application%2Fvnd.oci.image.manifest.v1%2Bjson&platform=linux%2Famd64&pullpolicy=missing&retry=3&retry-delay=2s&rewritetimestamp=0&rm=1&shmsize=67108864&t=perfcontainer": io: read/write on closed pipe
```

A normal `podman run` works:

```sh
$ podman run --rm --platform linux/amd64 -it fedora uname -a
Linux 54be182d3f2c 7.1.3-200.fc44.aarch64 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Sat Jul  4 19:23:52 UTC 2026 x86_64 GNU/Linux
```

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1. `podman machine init --cpus 4 --memory 10240 --disk-size 100`
2. `podman machine start`
3. `podman system connection default podman-machine-default-root`
4. Containerfile:
   ```
   FROM fedora
   RUN dnf install -y perf runc procps-ng binutils less lsof psmisc sysstat vim zip util-linux && dnf clean all
   ```
5. `podman build --platform linux/amd64 -t perfcontainer .`

Same issue with `--platform linux/arm64`. Also tried [Rosetta](https://blog.podman.io/2025/08/podman-5-6-released-rosetta-status-update/) but that didn't help.

### Describe the results you received

```

ERRO[0679] failed to close build request body: 1 error occurred:
	* open /Users/kevin/Library/Application Support/FileProvider/19467A89-FC03-40AE-BEAB-3D004245812B/wharf/tombstone/a: permission denied

 
Error: Post "http://d/v6.0.2/libpod/build?compressionFormat=gzip&dockerfile=%5B%22Containerfile%22%5D&forceCompressionFormat=1&forcerm=1&httpproxy=1&idmappingoptions=%7B%22HostUIDMapping%22%3Atrue%2C%22HostGIDMapping%22%3Atrue%2C%22UIDMap%22%3A%5B%5D%2C%22GIDMap%22%3A%5B%5D%2C%22AutoUserNs%22%3Afalse%2C%22AutoUserNsOpts%22%3A%7B%22Size%22%3A0%2C%22InitialSize%22%3A0%2C%22PasswdFile%22%3A%22%22%2C%22GroupFile%22%3A%22%22%2C%22AdditionalUIDMappings%22%3Anull%2C%22AdditionalGIDMappings%22%3Anull%7D%7D&inheritannotations=1&isolation=0&jobs=1&layers=1&networkmode=0&nsoptions=%5B%7B%22Name%22%3A%22user%22%2C%22Host%22%3Atrue%2C%22Path%22%3A%22%22%7D%5D&omithistory=0&output=perfcontainer&outputformat=application%2Fvnd.oci.image.manifest.v1%2Bjson&platform=linux%2Famd64&pullpolicy=missing&retry=3&retry-delay=2s&rewritetimestamp=0&rm=1&shmsize=67108864&t=perfcontainer": io: read/write on closed pipe
```

I think the issue is that the build context directory is located inside a folder managed by macOS FileProvider (likely iCloud Drive's Desktop & Documents sync), where files are replaced with placeholders that require special framework access to read. When Podman's client-side nTar function walks the build context to create a tarball, it calls `os.Open()` on these files and gets permission denied, producing a truncated tar stream that breaks the HTTP request to the machine VM.

Well, you are mixing two separate concepts:

- `-v` for mounting a directory into the VM via `podman machine init/set` (personally, I wouldn't change the machine defaults).
- `-v` for mounting a directory into a container via `podman run` (on macOS, this leverages mounts from the VM).

Another consideration is `podman build`. On Linux, macOS, and Windows, it requires a context directory. In your build command, you specified `.`, which means your current working directory (`pwd`). If you run that from `~/`, the instruction `COPY .  .` will attempt to copy your entire home directory into the container image.

On macOS, the implementation uses two mechanisms to access the context directory:

- Local API: This approach leverages directories already mounted to the Podman machine. It accesses files through VirtIO-FS, which is much faster than transferring the entire directory over the REST API.

- Fallback: If the directory isn't mounted, it creates a tarball of the entire directory and sends it to the Podman machine over the network via the REST API. 

Regarding the context directory, it's good practice to use a `.containerignore` file to exclude unnecessary files from the build context, especially when falling back to the REST API.

I don't think a warning is necessary since the local API is used most of the time, and podman build is already properly documented. I think we can close this issue.
